dod_intent_evidence: HigherGov federal awardee profile (News section) shows an active federal award record (most recent 2026-03-09) and channel notes describe Walaris supporting Honeywell in U.S. Air Force Global Strike Command / STRIKEWERX counter-UAS prototype testing; own-language LinkedIn-about names 'government' customers.
score_evidence: 'running billions of computations in real-time to identify known patterns or objects' / 'Novel artificial intelligence and computer vision algorithms' → lab_language_intensity

'seamlessly integrated with third-party sensors and command-and-control systems through its easy-to-use API' — no ATO/RMF/IL4-5/STIG/CMMC language anywhere despite protecting 'bases... government facilities' → deployment_awareness_absence (capped at 12: own-language word count ~966, under 1000)

own words repeatedly reference operators directly ('triggering real-time alerts to operators', 'with operator instruction', 'allowing operators to move confidently') — operators are not absent, so score is low

blind_spots.blind_spot: 'Real-time' billions-of-computations sensor fusion assumes continuous sensor throughput to the processing node.
blind_spots.operator_reality: Same failure mode as the canonical 30fps crowd-detection case: if AirScout's edge box loses link to a subset of its sensor array in a DDIL environment, the 'real-time fusion' claim has no described degraded mode.
blind_spots.why_likely_missing: Marketing emphasizes raw AI throughput as the differentiator rather than graceful degradation under contested comms.
blind_spots.evidence_quote: AirScout locally fuses data from deployed sensors, running billions of computations in real-time to identify known patterns or objects.

blind_spots.blind_spot: Protects 'bases, borders, government facilities' with zero accreditation vocabulary in any public page.
blind_spots.operator_reality: Sensor-fusion software touching base perimeter defense will need an ATO/RMF path onto government networks before it can go from prototype test to program of record; none of that language exists publicly.
blind_spots.why_likely_missing: Company is EO/IR-detection-first and commercial-market-broad (marine, critical infrastructure, stadiums), so compliance messaging hasn't been built out for the DoD-specific buyer.
blind_spots.evidence_quote: AirScout is utilized to protect sensitive locations across the globe, including bases, borders, government facilities, critical infrastructure, sports stadiums, and more.

blind_spots.blind_spot: API-first integration story with third-party sensors and C2 systems never addresses GFE integration mechanics or prime flow-down structure, despite supporting Honeywell on a USAF program.
blind_spots.operator_reality: Integrating into a prime's existing C2 stack under government data-rights and export-control terms is a different problem than a generic 'easy-to-use API' — ITAR handling for EO/IR targeting data isn't mentioned once.
blind_spots.why_likely_missing: Language optimized for commercial system integrators as a channel, not for the specific mechanics of subcontracting under a prime on a DoD prototype effort.
blind_spots.evidence_quote: AirScout's hardware-agnostic software can be rapidly upgraded or downgraded with different sensors or optics and seamlessly integrated with third-party sensors and command-and-control systems through its easy-to-use API.

opener_hook: Walaris' AirScout supported Honeywell's STRIKEWERX counter-UAS prototype testing for Global Strike Command — the harder part after a successful demo is usually the ATO, not the detection accuracy.
what_they_do: AI-driven EO/IR sensor-fusion software (AirScout) for counter-UAS detection, classification, and tracking at the edge, for airspace and perimeter defense.
